events.title: Publication of the First Fascicle of the Oxford English Dictionary
events.description: The first installment of the Oxford English Dictionary, then titled A New English Dictionary on Historical Principles, was published under editor James Murray, covering words from 'A' to 'Ant'.
events.significance: It marked the start of the monumental project that became the definitive historical record of the English language, taking until 1928 to complete in full.

events.title: Edison Completes the Black Maria Studio
events.description: Thomas Edison's Black Maria, the first motion picture production studio, was completed in West Orange, New Jersey. Around this time, Edison's lab also produced Fred Ott's Sneeze, one of the earliest films copyrighted in the United States.
events.significance: The studio laid the foundation for the American film industry and early motion picture production.

events.title: Ayatollah Khomeini Returns to Iran
events.description: After nearly 15 years in exile, Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini returned to Tehran to a massive welcome, as the Shah had left the country two weeks earlier.
events.significance: His return led to the collapse of the Pahlavi monarchy and the establishment of the Islamic Republic of Iran, reshaping Middle Eastern geopolitics.

events.title: Space Shuttle Columbia Disaster
events.description: Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrated during re-entry over Texas and Louisiana at the end of mission STS-107, killing all seven crew members. Damage from foam insulation striking the left wing during launch was the cause.
events.significance: The tragedy led to a major investigation, reforms in NASA safety culture, and the eventual retirement of the Space Shuttle program in 2011.

events.title: Thirteenth Amendment Passed by Congress and Signed by Lincoln
events.description: President Abraham Lincoln signed the joint resolution approving the Thirteenth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, abolishing slavery, and sent it to the states for ratification.
events.significance: The amendment, ratified in December 1865, formally abolished slavery and involuntary servitude in the United States, except as punishment for a crime.
